card.name: The word just after a verb
card.fires_on: The word "just" (sometimes "Still") right after a form of "to be" or similar, before "a" or "as", in web prose that minimizes or equates something.

modes.label: "just a" after is/are
modes.description: "just" follows is, are or can be and introduces a small or simple description.
modes.example: "The glacier is<< just>> a big dirty snowball," says Stephanie

modes.label: Sentence-initial "Still"
modes.description: "Still" opens a sentence or fragment, in a contrasting sense.
modes.example: http://www.mypcprogram.com/FrontPage.aspx -<< Still>> have computers with Windows XP or Vista.

card.writes: It slightly favors contrast and transition words, but the effect is mixed.
card.plain: It fires on the word "just" after "is" or "are", as in "it is just a matter of time".
